articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Sept. 23

Sources: Status of Mavs big man Lively up in air

Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress. Dallas begins training camp on Saturday.

Extension unlikely as Knicks, Towns talks stall

Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Vincent Goodwill on Wednesday.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

Sept. 22

Charania: Hield, Nembhard to Charlotte for Finney-Smith

The Atlanta Hawks are trading Dorian Finney-Smith to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension

The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

articles.headline: Red Sox's Ceddanne Rafaela injures hamstring in IL return
articles.description: Ceddanne Rafaela, who returned Wednesday after being sidelined since Sept. 3 with a right quad strain, left in the third inning with tightness in his right hamstring.
articles.body:
BOSTON -- Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who came off the injured list on Wednesday, left the game against the Cleveland Guardians in the third inning after pulling up while running out a single in the second.

Rafaela, who started and made a diving catch on the game's first batter, has been sidelined since Sept. 3 with a right quad strain.

The team announced that he left with right hamstring tightness.

He singled off the Green Monster in the second inning and came up lame at the first-base bag. He was visited by manager Chad Tracy and a trainer, jogged a bit down the right-field foul line and stayed in the game.

He then trotted out to his position for the top of the third but came walking off. He was replaced by Jarren Duran.

Rafaela, who won his first Gold Glove last season, made a headlong dive to rob Steven Kwan in right center on the third pitch of the game. He handled all three putouts the first inning.

He was batting .284 with with 16 homers and 70 RBIs coming into Wednesday's game.

To make room for him, the club optioned INF/OF Nate Eaton to Triple-A Worcester before the game.

articles.headline: Sources: Mavs' Dereck Lively II (foot) not cleared for camp
articles.description: Dereck Lively II's status for the start of the season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources said.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the past 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress.

Dallas begins training camp Saturday.

Lively has played a total of only 43 games in the past two seasons. He underwent his second surgery in December, ending his 2025-26 campaign after appearing in only seven games.

Lively, 22, the No. 12 pick in the 2023 draft, is entering the final season of his rookie contract.

If healthy, the 7-foot-1, 230-pound Lively could be a significant part of Dallas' long-term core as the Mavericks attempt to build a contender around reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

Lively, an athletic big man who is an excellent finisher and versatile defender, has career averages of 8.4 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 22.9 minutes per game.

articles.headline: Herbert shuts down leadership questions amid Chargers' 0-2 start
articles.description: Justin Herbert was uncharacteristically fiery when asked Wednesday about increased vocal leadership on the Chargers amid the team's 0-2 start.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- After being asked for a second time Wednesday about increased vocal leadership on the Los Angeles Chargers amid the team's 0-2 start, quarterback Justin Herbert -- seemingly annoyed by the premise -- cut the question off.

"I don't think there's a lack of vocal leadership at all. So, I'm going to stop you right there and say that it's very present," he said. "I don't think anyone is panicked or worried because that's not going to be the sentiment. It's moving on to the next play and understand that we're close, we've made mistakes, how do we fix it?"

It was a rare moment of vulnerability and passion for Herbert, whose answers usually are laden with recycled football platitudes. Herbert was somewhat fiery in his first answer to the question, too.

"I think that would imply that there's no need for vocal leadership before this week," he said. "I think every week is a super important week for us and it's a great opportunity for us to go play football again and correct the things that we made mistakes on last week and keep pushing forward."

The Bolts are off to a surprising start with losses to two of the worst teams in the NFL last season in the Las Vegas Raiders and Arizona Cardinals, who had the first and third picks in the draft, respectively.

In both defeats, the Chargers offense -- which was projected to be among the league's best with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel -- looked helplessly lost. Sunday's 26-14 setback to the Raiders saw a rare outburst from Herbert after a late snap hit wide receiver Tre' Harris' legs and resulted in a fourth down.

Herbert slammed his fists and yelled at his teammates as he exited the field.

Herbert hasn't directly answered for the outburst, deflecting after the game and again Wednesday, resorting to football cliches: "I think it's always just about the next play." But he doesn't really have to address his on-field frustrations; it's clear he is irritated with the way this offense has performed.

Coach Jim Harbaugh called the offense's struggles "growing pains," saying that he felt like the team was letting Herbert down. He pointed to Herbert's two interceptions against the Raiders, both by cornerback Hezekiah Masses: One was bobbled by tight end David Njoku and into Masses' hands and the other he said came because wide receiver Derius Davis ran the wrong route.

"I wouldn't change anything about Justin," Harbaugh said.

The Chargers will look to get back on track Sunday when they travel to Buffalo to take on the Bills.

"At no point is anyone going to say ... it's time to panic or anything like that," Herbert said. "It's about playing football, about the next play and doing your job."

articles.headline: Stanton, Grisham take steps toward rejoining Yankees
articles.description: Yankees slugger Giancarlo Stanton could return for the playoffs after a 5½-month absence due to calf strains.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Yankees slugger Giancarlo Stanton could return for the playoffs after a 5½-month absence due to calf strains.

Stanton faced pitchers Wednesday at Double-A Somerset along with center fielder Trent Grisham, sidelined since straining his right hamstring on Sept. 4. Both ran the bases and Stanton homered while taking six or seven at-bats.

"Putting them on the outskirts of the conversation," New York manager Aaron Boone, bothered by a cold, said in a raspy voice.

Already without injured star Aaron Judge because of a strained right calf, New York is likely to host Boston in a best-of-three American League Wild Card Series starting Tuesday, with all three games at Yankee Stadium.

Following the end of the seasons for Yankees farm teams, New York has minor leaguers working out at Somerset in nearby New Jersey.

Stanton hasn't played since April 24 because of strained calf muscles in both legs after starting the season with a .256 batting average, three homers and 14 RBIs in 24 games. The 36-year-old former National League MVP had 38 homers and 100 RBIs in his first season with New York in 2018 but has missed 500 of 1,194 games since (41.9%), through the end of this regular season.

His other injuries included strains of his right biceps, right knee, left hamstring (three times), left quadriceps and both calf muscles along with right ankle inflammation, left Achilles tendinitis and tendon pain in both elbows.

"You're looking more at a pinch-hit scenario," Boone said. "We'll see if that's even a realistic option."

Stanton is owed $25 million next year in the final guaranteed season of a $325 million, 13-year contract that includes a $10 million buyout of a 2028 club option.

Also, Carlos Lagrange, a 23-year-old right-hander who reached 100 mph with 98 pitches at Triple-A this year, threw to batters at Somerset. He was out between June 28 and Sept. 16 because of a right capsule strain.

Lagrange was shifted to the bullpen at the start of June.

"He's in the conversation for something," Boone said.

Right-hander Clarke Schmidt, who returned Sept. 16 following Tommy John surgery in July 2025, played catch but remains sidelined by right biceps cramps. New York had hoped to use him as a reliever in the postseason.

"Today was better than yesterday," Boone said. "If he's not a real viable option by tomorrow, then we'll probably go a different way."

Boone said Cam Schlittler will start Game 1 or 2 of the playoffs. Max Fried appears set to start whichever game Schlittler doesn't, with Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón available for Game 3.

"Whoever goes 1 or 2 can pitch 2 and 5 in the next series," Boone said.

Right-hander Fernando Cruz threw a bullpen this week and is to throw another one Thursday.

He hasn't pitched in a game since Aug. 25 because of right elbow discomfort caused by a partially torn ulnar collateral ligament.

"I'm in a really good position to be back I will say in the next couple of weeks," Cruz said.

articles.headline: Blue Jays' Guerrero stands by comments about contract extension
articles.description: Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is standing by comments he made during a recent interview regarding his performance this season after signing a 14-year, $500 million contract last year.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is standing by comments he made during a recent interview regarding his performance this season after signing a 14-year, $500 million contract last year.

In an interview with Spanish-language reporter Veronica Batista, Guerrero was asked about his struggles in the first season after signing a 14-year, $500 million extension with the Blue Jays in April, 2025. Guerrero told Batista that he was being paid for what he had done in the past, not what he was going to do in the future.

The comments received backlash from fans.

"I want people to understand one thing. The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did," Guerrero told Batista. "They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 [home runs] every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself, 'Bro, they gave you all that money and you're out here doing nothing.' But I try.

"You know how it is with fans, when you're good, they're with you 100%. But when you smell like s---, like we like to say here, nobody supports you. The ones who support you are the ones who stay with you. Those are my real fans and I considered them my family."

Asked about those comments following the Blue Jays being eliminated from playoff contention Wednesday afternoon, Guerrero stood by them.

"No, I don't regret myself. I'm not lying with what I say," Guerrero said through an interpreter. "I understand some fans, they don't understand the way and what I was trying to say specifically, but what I said is the way I feel."

Guerrero is having one of his worst seasons at the plate, entering Wednesday hitting .263 with nine home runs and 56 RBIs in 140 games.

articles.headline: Veteran Case Keenum practices Wednesday, ready to start if called
articles.description: Bears veteran QB Case Keenum could be in line to start his first regular-season game since 2023. "If my name's called, I'm excited to be out there," he said.
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- The Chicago Bears aren't certain who will start at quarterback against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3, but 15-year journeyman Case Keenum is next up after a rash of injuries have decimated the quarterback room.

Keenum was the only quarterback on the Bears' active roster to practice Wednesday while Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Tyson Bagent (concussion) were sidelined. Miller Moss, an undrafted rookie on Chicago's practice squad, took backup reps during the two-hour session.

Five days removed from Chicago's primetime showdown on "Monday Night Football," Keenum could be in line to start his first regular-season game since 2023.

"I feel very prepared," Keenum said. "It's what I do every week. It's what I've done for a long time. I've backed up a long time in this league. If my name's called, I'm excited to be out there."

Keenum, 38, has not played in a regular-season NFL game since Weeks 15 and 16 of the 2023 season when he logged consecutive starts for the Houston Texans. As the Bears' third-string quarterback behind Williams and Bagent, Keenum's practice cadence is normally restricted to mental reps, which he's exchanging this week for work with the starters.

"I feel as good mentally as I've ever felt," Keenum said. "Being able to see things before they happen, having a lot of banked reps. So stuff I've done in the past, maybe we're not getting a ton of reps of it this week, but feel good about if I'm playing to be the one to run those plays. I think as far as operationally goes, I think we can do a lot of things pre-snap, try to get the right play when we can, and I think we can do a lot of fun stuff."

Keenum ended up in this position after Bagent reported concussion symptoms Tuesday and entered the league's five-step protocol. Coach Ben Johnson said he believes Bagent was injured on the backup's second play in place of Williams in the fourth quarter. After releasing a short pass to his left that fell incomplete, Bagent was tackled by Vikings outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel.

Bagent was not present at Halas Hall on Wednesday while working through the earliest phase of the concussion protocol. Meanwhile, Williams, who is classified as week-to-week, has been actively involved in walk-throughs and meetings as the Bears game-plan for the Eagles.

Earlier this week, coach Ben Johnson said Williams is not expected to practice but did not rule him out for Week 3. The Bears do not plan to sign another quarterback in the meantime.

Despite the uncertainty of their quarterback situation, Johnson views the challenge of so many unknowns as an opportunity.

"One of those things that everyone outside the building I am sure is writing us off and telling us it can't be done and we really relish that," Johnson said. "So, guys will step up to the plate, guys that maybe we don't anticipate or expect."

articles.headline: Broncos RB Coleman doesn't practice; Dobbins, Harvey limited
articles.description: Broncos running backs J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey were limited in practice Wednesday, and Jonah Coleman did not practice. Nevertheless, coach Sean Payton said he thinks "we're going to be all right" at the position Sunday against the Rams.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Ahead of a primetime matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, the Denver Broncos practiced Wednesday with three of their four running backs either limited or out of practice, with coach Sean Payton saying he still hoped for the best.

J.K. Dobbins, who left Sunday's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury, and RJ Harvey, who did not play Sunday because of a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, were both limited in practice.

And rookie Jonah Coleman did not practice. Coleman sprained an ankle during Sunday's game, but he stayed in the lineup and was the running back on the field to help the Broncos seal the win. He had 33 of his 39 rushing yards, including two 12-yard runs, on the Broncos' final possession, when the offense used up the final 4:41 on the clock.

Asked Wednesday if he had concerns about the position heading into Sunday's game, Payton didn't offer details about the injuries but added, "I think we're good at that position ... I think we're going to be all right.''

Tyler Badie was the only running back on the active roster who was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Fullback Adam Prentice and running back Cody Schrader, the team's leading rusher in the preseason, are on the Broncos' practice squad.

Coleman, a fourth-round pick in the 2026 draft, had his first career touchdown on a 3-yard run against the Jaguars. He has received treatment on the injured ankle over the past three days and that will continue through the week.

Dobbins, who leads the Broncos in carries (18) and yards rushing (72) through two games, missed seven games in 2025 after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 10. He had issued a "pinkie swear'' promise in training camp that he would play every game this season.

The Broncos did work out three running backs Tuesday -- Jaden Nixon, Sam Scott and Marcus Yarns -- but as of Wednesday had not signed any of the three.

Prentice has already been elevated from the practice squad twice this season for games, so he has one more elevation remaining before the Broncos would have to sign him to the roster to have him available for games.

articles.headline: Counsell says Cubs at disadvantage after schedule change
articles.description: Cubs manager Craig Counsell was quick to point out the disadvantages his team faces this weekend after the league moved Sunday's contest against the Boston Red Sox to Friday due to a poor weather forecast.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Cubs manager Craig Counsell was quick to point out the disadvantages his team faces this weekend after the league moved Sunday's contest against the Boston Red Sox to Friday due to a poor weather forecast. It means the two teams will play a doubleheader that night then conclude their regular seasons Saturday.

"They never move games up and especially within a five-day window of a starting rotation," Counsell said Wednesday. "So we can't have somebody ready to pitch on Saturday. They just moved games up on us. I understand there's extenuating circumstances, but you just don't see that happening."

Under normal circumstances, a rainout would force a doubleheader the next day, actually giving teams an extra day of rest for the starter of the postponed game. In this case, the Cubs will have to move Saturday's starter to Friday, leaving Game 162 in flux for them on the mound -- assuming weather doesn't cause havoc to Friday or Saturday's game in the first place.

It's likely lefty starter Shota Imanaga will pitch on short rest if Saturday's game is played as scheduled.

"What I know is happening is we're going to play three games," Counsell said. "So if weather is an issue, then yeah, we're going to have to figure out a place to play a third game."

The league discussed all options for the series as neither team wants to play Monday while moving it altogether to another city is a last resort. Both teams are likely to be in the postseason which starts Tuesday. Boston has already clinched a spot while the Cubs' magic number is one entering their contest against the Miami Marlins on Wednesday evening.

But seeding -- and home field advantage -- is still to be determined thus making the weekend series an important one. Adding some annoyance for Chicago is the fact that their season could be done while their closest competitors would have two more games to play, and league rules don't allow for an extra rostered player for September doubleheaders, further putting a burden on their pitching staff.

"The decision is made always on a balance of everybody's interest," Counsell stated. "And you get shortchanged in some ... or not have the optimal solution."

Meanwhile, Counsell is hopeful to have third baseman Alex Bregman in a game against his former team this weekend. Bregman spoke publicly for the first time Wednesday since getting hit in the left cheek by a foul ball while on-deck Sunday.

"It felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face," Bregman said. "The left side of my face has been numb. As soon as the swelling goes down, I'm sure I'll feel the breaks a little bit more."

Bregman's left eye is blood red while his cheek is still swollen but getting better. He said he can see fine and will continue to work his way back one "step at a time."

"There's a lot of fluid in my face over there," he explained. "If I move, the fluid moves. So if I'm bouncing up and down, my face feels like it's bouncing up and down."

articles.headline: UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped
articles.description: A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.
articles.body:
A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.

The Prime Minister said it was unfair for football fans to be singled out when supporters of other sports were able to drink while watching their teams.

The ban was put in place during the 1980s when concerns about hooliganism were at their height and covers the top-five tiers of English men's football.

But Everton fan Mr. Burnham said it was a measure from "an era when football was very different."

The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) welcomed the Prime Minister's words and said successful pilots of alcohol in the stands had been carried out in the women's game.

But police chiefs warned it would be "incredibly rash" to make changes without proper consultation with forces.

Mr. Burnham told reporters: "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point.

"I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.

"And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis.

"But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently from others."

The Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol) Act 1985 prohibits drinking in sight of the pitch in England and Wales in the top-five men's leagues.

FSA chairman Tom Greatrex said: "The FSA has always argued that it's unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match -- especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league.

"Many clubs are in favour as well. WSL and WSL2 ran a successful pilot, meaning fans can now drink in the stands at many grounds, while the EFL has long supported a trial.

"We welcome the Prime Minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed. We look forward to being part of that consultation."

A UK Football Policing Unit spokesman said police chiefs would welcome a meeting with Mr. Burnham to "explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans."

The spokesman said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour.

"It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games.

"Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor Report for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster.

articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズのスター、ステフィン・カリーは、未解決の契約延長交渉の状況が自身のプレーやシーズン開幕を迎えるチームの雰囲気に影響を与えることは一切ないと語った。

articles.headline: Man United transfer strategy 'financial sustainable' as losses increase - CEO
articles.description: Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after reporting a increased financial losses.
articles.headlineJa: 赤字拡大もマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの移籍戦略は「財政的に持続可能」とCEOが主張
articles.descriptionJa: 赤字の拡大が報告されたのを受け、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのオマル・ベラダCEOは、今夏の移籍戦略は「財政的な持続可能性を念頭に置いたもの」だったと述べた。
